findings.claim: `@experimental` is replaced by `@default true` for `staticParse`, asserting static parsing is on by default — this should be verified against actual config resolution, and it silently promotes an experimental flag to stable API.
findings.rationale: `staticParse?: boolean` is optional, so the documented default only holds if the resolver actually falls back to `true` (e.g. `staticParse ?? true`). If resolution still defaults to `false`/undefined, the doc is wrong and callers will assume static collection when it isn't happening. Dropping `@experimental` is also a stability commitment: if the flag can still change or be removed, that signal is lost for users and for tooling that keys on the tag. Moderate confidence — I cannot see the resolution code from this hunk.

findings.claim: `@default os.availableParallelism()` for `staticParseConcurrency` may not match the real default, and `os.availableParallelism()` is unavailable on Node < 18.14/19.4.
findings.rationale: Two concerns. (1) Accuracy: the documented default must match the resolver; implementations often use `os.cpus().length`, `availableParallelism() - 1`, or a fixed cap, which would make this misleading for anyone tuning concurrency. (2) Portability: `os.availableParallelism` only exists from Node 18.14/19.4 onward, so if the implementation calls it without a fallback it throws on older supported Node versions, and the doc now advertises that exact call. Also worth confirming the resolver guards against `0`/negative/non-integer user values, since `0` concurrency could stall parsing. Medium confidence — only the JSDoc is visible here.
